stemMd: A warehouse in Novara gives each of its 300 shelf positions a different code. Every code is a binary number written with the same, fixed number of bits. What is the smallest number of bits that makes this possible?
explanationMd:
A code of $n$ bits can take $2^{n}$ different values, so the shortest usable length is the smallest $n$ with $2^{n} \ge 300$.

Powers of two: $2^{8} = 256$ and $2^{9} = 512$.

With 8 bits there are only 256 codes, which is fewer than the 300 positions. With 9 bits there are 512 codes, which is enough. The smallest number of bits is 9.

**Check.** Both sides of the boundary: 8 bits fail because $256 < 300$, and 9 bits succeed because $512 \ge 300$. Nothing smaller than 9 can work, since fewer bits give even fewer codes.

distractorRationale.a: Uses a single byte, which is the habit for storing a small number, but 8 bits give only $2^{8} = 256$ codes and 300 are needed.
distractorRationale.c: Rounds up to $2^{10} = 1024$ as a safe size. That works, but it is not the smallest: 9 bits already give 512 codes.
distractorRationale.d: Divides 300 by 8, mixing up bits and bytes. The number of bits needed grows with the logarithm of the count, not in proportion to it.
distractorRationale.e: Uses one bit for each position. A code of $n$ bits can distinguish $2^{n}$ things, not just $n$ things.

accessibilityText: A question on bits. A warehouse gives each of its 300 shelf positions a different binary code, all codes having the same fixed number of bits. The smallest possible number of bits is wanted. The choices are 8, 9, 10, 38 and 300.

provenance.notes: Original item. Wrong choices: one byte, the next round power of two, bits confused with bytes, one bit per item.

independentSolve.workingNotes: 2^8=256 < 300 <= 512=2^9, so 9 bits is the smallest number that works. 8 bits is too few. 10 bits works but is not the smallest, and 38 and 300 are nonsense distractors. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tili-phys-tech-run9) reached the same answer: 2^8=256<300<=512=2^9, so 9 bits is the minimum. 8 is too few, 10 works but is not smallest, 38 and 300 are arbitrary.]
